title: Standing Architectural Rules & Ledger Schema
description: General JSON Schema defining standing architectural rules, Firebase security invariants, and verification contracts for mechanical issue ledgers.

$schema.description: URI or relative path of the schema governing this document.

title.description: Imperative summary of the architectural violation or defect.

screenshot.description: Optional artifact filename or URL of the visual evidence/review.

rule.description: Canonical standing architectural rule or recognized alias being enforced.

target.description: The exact source code location containing the violation.

file.description: Relative path to the primary file under review from the project root.

secondaryFile.description: Optional relative path to a secondary file affected by the violation.

enclosingSymbol.description: Function, class, or module enclosing the target violation.

anchor.description: Contextual anchor to locate the code snippet precisely.

violation.description: The defect narrative and required architectural remediation.

problem.description: Detailed explanation of what rule is violated and why.

expectedSolution.description: The exact architectural remediation required to close the issue.

forbiddenPatterns.description: Strings or tokens that MUST NOT appear in the target files for the issue to be marked fixed.

requiredPatterns.description: Strings or tokens that MUST appear in the target files for the issue to be marked fixed.

ALLOWLIST_NORMALIZED_SELF_LOOKUP_RULES.summary: Gate account profile creation and reads on a verified, lowercase-normalized email allowlist lookup with self-only read and no collection enumeration.
ALLOWLIST_NORMALIZED_SELF_LOOKUP_RULES.description: Any authenticated Google OAuth user can currently create and read `users/{uid}` without allowlist membership. Furthermore, allowlist documents must be keyed by lowercase email (`allowlist/{email}`), require `request.auth.token['email_verified'] == true` via `hasClaim('email')`, permit `get` only when `request.auth.token['email'].lower() == email`, deny `list` and `write`, and regenerate `studio/firestore.rules` from `studio/firestore.modules.rules`.
ALLOWLIST_NORMALIZED_SELF_LOOKUP_RULES.remediation: Import `hasClaim` from `'membership'`, define `hasVerifiedEmail()` and `isAllowlisted()` using `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/allowlist/$(request.auth.token['email'].lower()))`, expose `/allowlist/{email}` with self-only `allow get` and `allow list, write: if false;`, gate `/users/{uid}` on `isAllowlisted()`, and resolve `studio/firestore.modules.rules` to `studio/firestore.rules`.

ALLOWLIST_MUTATION_BOUNDARY_PARITY.summary: Require `isAllowlisted()` across all user-authored Firestore collection mutations (`narrations` and `playlists`) and maintain modular build parity.
ALLOWLIST_MUTATION_BOUNDARY_PARITY.description: Gating `users/{uid}` alone leaves a privilege gap where a non-allowlisted or revoked Firebase Auth user can still directly invoke Firestore `create`, `update`, or `delete` on `narrations/{narrationId}` and `playlists/{playlistId}` if they only check `isOwner(...)`.
ALLOWLIST_MUTATION_BOUNDARY_PARITY.remediation: Require `isAllowlisted()` on `create`, `update`, and `delete` in both `match /narrations/{narrationId}` and `match /playlists/{playlistId}` in `studio/firestore.modules.rules`, then regenerate `studio/firestore.rules` via `pyric firestore rules resolve`.

ADMIN_SDK_ALLOWLIST_ENFORCEMENT.summary: Server Admin SDK token verification must enforce verified email and Firestore allowlist membership before returning a caller UID.
ADMIN_SDK_ALLOWLIST_ENFORCEMENT.description: Because `adminDb()` and `adminBucket()` bypass Firestore and Storage Security Rules completely, returning `decoded.uid` from `verifyIdToken` without checking `decoded.email_verified === true` and `adminDb().collection('allowlist').doc(email).get()` allows non-allowlisted or revoked users to trigger Gemini TTS synthesis (`POST /api/narrations`) and mutate server-managed resources.
antiPatterns:
const decoded = await adminAuth().verifyIdToken(token.trim(), true);
    return decoded.uid;
ADMIN_SDK_ALLOWLIST_ENFORCEMENT.remediation: In `verifyIdToken` (`studio/src/lib/firebase-admin.ts`), normalize `decoded.email?.trim().toLowerCase()`, verify `decoded.email_verified === true`, and confirm `(await adminDb().collection('allowlist').doc(email).get()).exists` before returning `decoded.uid`.

CLIENT_AUTH_ALLOWLIST_GATE.summary: Client AuthProvider must verify `allowlist/{email}` membership with session guarding before provisioning `users/{uid}` or mounting the signed-in shell.
CLIENT_AUTH_ALLOWLIST_GATE.description: When `onAuthStateChanged` emits a `firebaseUser`, immediately calling `upsertUserProfile` and `onSnapshot(userRef(uid))` without first verifying `allowlist/{email}` causes non-allowlisted users to enter the app shell with denied writes and unguarded async state transitions, while `SignInGate` gives no feedback that account creation is allowlist-restricted.
antiPatterns: New here? Continuing with Google creates your account.
CLIENT_AUTH_ALLOWLIST_GATE.remediation: Guard the async auth transition with a session counter (`loadSessionRef.current++`), check `isEmailAllowlisted(nextUser.email)` against `allowlist/{email}` before calling `upsertUserProfile` or attaching `onSnapshot`, sign out non-allowlisted users (`await signOut(auth())`), expose `accessDenied` on `AuthState`, and render an explicit allowlist denial notice in `SignInGate`.

NO_SILENT_ERROR_SWALLOWING.summary: Catch blocks must log, rethrow, or handle errors explicitly.
NO_SILENT_ERROR_SWALLOWING.description: Empty catch blocks and silent error suppression hide bugs, race conditions, and corrupted state.
NO_SILENT_ERROR_SWALLOWING.remediation: Handle expected errors with specific condition checks, or rethrow with contextual wrapping.

REQUIRE_NAMED_BOOLEANS.summary: Replace compound inline conditions with self-documenting const booleans.
REQUIRE_NAMED_BOOLEANS.description: Nested inline boolean logic increases cognitive load and hides branch conditions.
REQUIRE_NAMED_BOOLEANS.remediation: Extract conditions into descriptive variables: const hasData = data.count > 0; const isReady = res.ok && !res.pending && (hasData || forced);

NO_BOOLEAN_COERCION_CHAINS.summary: Eliminate double-negation or nested Boolean(...) coercion chains.
NO_BOOLEAN_COERCION_CHAINS.description: Chains like Boolean(Boolean(x)) or !!Boolean(x) obscure the underlying value and type contract.
NO_BOOLEAN_COERCION_CHAINS.remediation: Use explicit equality checks or a single Boolean(x) / !!x.

ATOMIC_FILE_OPERATIONS.summary: Prevent TOCTOU file system race conditions using atomic file descriptor flags.
ATOMIC_FILE_OPERATIONS.description: Checking fs.existsSync() immediately before fs.writeFileSync() creates a time-of-check to time-of-use vulnerability.
ATOMIC_FILE_OPERATIONS.remediation: Use atomic openSync with O_CREAT | O_EXCL and catch EEXIST, or write via atomic rename.

ZERO_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBILITY.summary: Zero backwards compatibility for unreleased software or deprecated internal paths.
ZERO_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBILITY.description: Retaining legacy shims, fallback paths, and compatibility layers for unreleased software introduces dead code and store bypasses.
ZERO_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBILITY.remediation: Purge legacy fallbacks completely. Standardize on the canonical store or path.

ADMIN_WRITE_OWNERSHIP_GUARD.summary: Admin SDK writes to user-owned documents must verify existing ownership inside a transaction before writing.
ADMIN_WRITE_OWNERSHIP_GUARD.description: Admin credentials bypass Security Rules. A route that writes a caller-chosen document id with `docRef.set(...)` lets one user overwrite and take ownership of another user's document. The Rules layer cannot observe or block this path, so the server must enforce ownership itself.
antiPatterns: activeStreams.set(id, { uid, abort: abortStream }); // without an owner check
ADMIN_WRITE_OWNERSHIP_GUARD.remediation: Reserve client-supplied ids with an ownership pre-check (`claimNarrationId`) that returns 409, and make the authoritative write a server transaction that refuses when `snap.data()?.ownerUid !== uid`. Never replace another uid's in-memory stream handle.

SERVER_DERIVED_STORAGE_PATHS.summary: Admin SDK Storage access must derive object paths from the authorized identity, never from client-writable document fields.
SERVER_DERIVED_STORAGE_PATHS.description: Routes that read `narration.audioPath` / `narration.timingsPath` and download with `adminBucket()` let an owner repoint their own document at another user's private object. This is a confused-deputy read that bypasses Storage Rules.
SERVER_DERIVED_STORAGE_PATHS.remediation: Build every server-side object path with `audioObjectPath(narration.ownerUid, id)` / `timingsObjectPath(narration.ownerUid, id)` after the document read has been authorized.

STORAGE_RULES_NO_STALE_METADATA_AUTH.summary: Storage Rules must not authorize reads from object metadata that is not kept in sync with the authoritative Firestore state.
STORAGE_RULES_NO_STALE_METADATA_AUTH.description: Object `metadata.visibility` is written once at synthesis time and never rewritten when the Firestore narration changes visibility. A `resource.metadata.visibility == 'public'` branch therefore keeps un-published audio publicly readable.
STORAGE_RULES_NO_STALE_METADATA_AUTH.remediation: Make client Storage reads owner-only (`allow read: if isOwner(ownerUid);`) and serve shared and public playback through server routes that authorize against the current Firestore document. Stop writing authorization-looking metadata.

CLIENT_WRITE_FIELD_ALLOWLIST.summary: Client updates must be limited to the keys the UI edits; documents created only by the server must refuse client creates.
CLIENT_WRITE_FIELD_ALLOWLIST.description: Update rules without `diff().affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` let an owner forge server-owned fields (status, durationMs, Storage paths, author snapshot) and add unknown keys. A client create rule on a server-created collection lets clients author complete documents with forged state.
antiPatterns:
allow create: if isAllowlisted()
        && isOwner(request.resource.data.ownerUid)
        && hasRequiredNarrationFields()
CLIENT_WRITE_FIELD_ALLOWLIST.remediation: Use `allow create: if false;` for server-created collections, and `request.resource.data.diff(resource.data).affectedKeys().hasOnly([...client-edited keys])` on client-updatable documents.

REAL_USER_READ_GATE.summary: Every non-public read must require an allowlisted account; only explicitly public documents are open to everyone.
REAL_USER_READ_GATE.description: Read rules that check only `isOwner` or `sharedWith` membership let non-allowlisted or de-allowlisted accounts read shared content and their own data directly from Firestore, even though the server (`verifyIdToken`) refuses them. Rules and server disagree.
REAL_USER_READ_GATE.remediation: Allow `visibility == 'public'` for anyone. Gate the owner and shared branches (and owner-only collections such as playlists) behind `isAllowlisted()`.

REPLAYABLE_REGRESSION_BOOTSTRAP.summary: Regression fixtures must carry their own bootstrap; hosted parity and operator bootstrap must be scripted and documented.
REPLAYABLE_REGRESSION_BOOTSTRAP.description: `pyric verify` replays from an empty database and only re-issues captured writes. State seeded out-of-band (for example allowlist documents written directly to the store) makes a correct capture fail on replay. Pyric-derived hosted cases omit `exists()` mocks. The production allowlist bootstrap (IAM → `studio:allowlist add`) is undocumented.
antiPatterns: Allowlist documents seeded outside the captured session
Committed fixtures containing real account emails
REPLAYABLE_REGRESSION_BOOTSTRAP.remediation: Record the allowlist bootstrap as admin writes inside the capture. Commit a synthetic-identity fixture with a `rules:verify` script. Add a mock-aware hosted harness (`rules:verify:hosted`), an operator runbook in `studio/README.md`, and upstream Pyric reports in `studio/PYRIC.md`.

NO_CLIENT_AI_ENDPOINTS.summary: Model calls run only on the server, behind the allowlisted identity check.
NO_CLIENT_AI_ENDPOINTS.description: Firebase AI Logic is reachable with the public web config and cannot check the Firestore allowlist; App Check attests the app, not the user. A client `getGenerativeModel`/`getAI` handle lets anyone spend Gemini quota.
NO_CLIENT_AI_ENDPOINTS.remediation: Remove `firebase/ai` from the client. Put any model feature behind a Cloud Run route that calls `verifyIdToken`. Leave AI Logic disabled in the console.

HERMETIC_DEPLOY_BUILD.summary: A clean clone must build the production image with no local-only artifacts, dev sandboxes, or secrets.
HERMETIC_DEPLOY_BUILD.description: `studio` installs `mdmedia` from a gitignored tarball outside its directory and Pyric from gitignored local tarballs, so a clean build cannot install. Dev-only wiring (Pyric register, sandbox URLs, browser Gemini keys) must never reach the production image.
antiPatterns: COPY of .env files or service-account JSON into the image
PYRIC_SANDBOX or @pyric/cli/register in the runtime environment
HERMETIC_DEPLOY_BUILD.remediation: Build and pack `mdmedia` inside the image, strip Pyric devDependencies before install, ignore secrets in `.dockerignore`, and gate deploys on a preflight script.

DEPLOY_RUNBOOK_LEAST_PRIVILEGE.summary: Deploys are documented, ordered rules-first, and run under a dedicated least-privilege identity with secrets in Secret Manager.
DEPLOY_RUNBOOK_LEAST_PRIVILEGE.description: There is no hosting config, no runtime identity, and no deploy order. Deploying the app before the hardened rules, or running with a key file or the default compute account, widens access.
antiPatterns: Default compute service account with Editor
DEPLOY_RUNBOOK_LEAST_PRIVILEGE.remediation: Hosting rewrites to Cloud Run; a dedicated service account with scoped roles; `GEMINI_API_KEY` via `--set-secrets`; deploy order preflight → rules → Cloud Run → Hosting, documented in `studio/README.md`.

SHARE_BY_RESOLVED_UID.summary: Share lists hold uids resolved server-side from allowlisted emails; the rules authorize on uid.
SHARE_BY_RESOLVED_UID.description: The share box writes emails into `sharedWith`, but the rules and `loadReadableNarration` check `request.auth.uid in sharedWith`, so sharing never grants access.
antiPatterns: Resolving emails to uids in the client
SHARE_BY_RESOLVED_UID.remediation: Resolve through `POST /api/users/resolve` (caller and target allowlisted), write the uid plus a `sharedWithLabels` display map, and allow `sharedWithLabels` in the update field allowlist.

LONG_REQUESTS_BYPASS_HOSTING.summary: Requests that can run longer than Hosting's rewrite limit go to Cloud Run directly, with origin-pinned CORS and recovery for interrupted work.
LONG_REQUESTS_BYPASS_HOSTING.description: Hosting cuts rewritten requests at 60 s while synthesis runs up to 300 s, and background work can be lost on scale-in or redeploy.
antiPatterns: Narrations left in status streaming forever
LONG_REQUESTS_BYPASS_HOSTING.remediation: POST to `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN`, allow only `ALLOWED_WEB_ORIGINS`, and mark stale `streaming` narrations as `error`/`interrupted`.

AUTH_BLOCKING_ALLOWLIST.summary: Accounts not on the allowlist never obtain a Firebase ID token.
AUTH_BLOCKING_ALLOWLIST.description: Any Google account can create a Firebase Auth user and receive a token; only rules and routes stop it afterwards.
antiPatterns: Relying only on post-sign-in checks for account creation
AUTH_BLOCKING_ALLOWLIST.remediation: Identity Platform blocking functions `beforeUserCreated` and `beforeUserSignedIn` reject unverified or non-allowlisted emails.

GRACE_PERIOD_STRICTMODE_HYGIENE.summary: Real-time subscriptions must maintain ref-counted or tokenized handles across React 18 StrictMode double-mount cycles.
GRACE_PERIOD_STRICTMODE_HYGIENE.description: Storing subscriber callbacks in a bare Set causes StrictMode remounts with identical callback references to collapse to a single entry. The first cleanup deletes the callback, reducing subscriber count to 0 and triggering grace-period detachment while the remounted component is active.
GRACE_PERIOD_STRICTMODE_HYGIENE.remediation: Track subscriptions by unique token/subscription ID handles or reference counters rather than bare callback sets. Ensure cleanup for one handle does not prematurely drop active sibling handles.

PROMPT_STYLE_DIRECTIVE_STRIPPING.summary: Non-spoken stage directions and bracketed prompt directives must be stripped before word alignment tokenization.
PROMPT_STYLE_DIRECTIVE_STRIPPING.description: Including bracketed style directives like [style: whisper] or [whisper] in word-alignment tokenization indexes non-spoken characters, pushes spoken words to offset indices, and steals vocal energy onset windows, misaligning transcript highlights.
antiPatterns: const regex = /\S+/g; // without stripping bracket directives
tokens.push({ wordIndex: index++, word, charStart, charEnd })
PROMPT_STYLE_DIRECTIVE_STRIPPING.remediation: Strip bracketed directives ([style: ...], [...]) before tokenizing spoken words or map spoken words to source document offsets without creating spoken tokens for directives.

TTS_WIRE_FRAME_ALIGNMENT.summary: Streaming audio payloads must enforce 2-byte 16-bit PCM frame alignment and strip WAV container headers.
TTS_WIRE_FRAME_ALIGNMENT.description: Streaming endpoints that emit odd-byte audio chunks split 16-bit PCM sample frames across network packets. Streaming players that fail to detect and strip 44-byte RIFF headers decode ASCII metadata as audible waveforms, causing loud pops and phase drift.
antiPatterns: queue.push({ type: 'audio', pcm: Buffer.from(copy).toString('base64') }); // unaligned odd bytes
TTS_WIRE_FRAME_ALIGNMENT.remediation: Enforce 2-byte sample alignment on all audio deltas, carry odd trailing bytes across frames, and strip 44-byte RIFF headers in streaming players before decoding samples.

SAFE_STREAM_HEADER_FINALIZATION.summary: Audio sinks must rewrite data lengths upon stream abort or error, or cleanly unlink incomplete files.
SAFE_STREAM_HEADER_FINALIZATION.description: Writing a 44-byte zeroed placeholder at the start of a WAV file and closing on stream abort/error without patching the header leaves corrupted, unplayable files with zeroed headers on disk or in Cloud Storage.
SAFE_STREAM_HEADER_FINALIZATION.remediation: Intercept abort and error events in audio file sinks to write createWavHeader with the actual bytesWritten, or unlink the incomplete file.

OPFS_RESILIENT_STORAGE_FAILOVER.summary: Media storage services must handle OPFS lock contention and quota exceptions with in-memory failover.
OPFS_RESILIENT_STORAGE_FAILOVER.description: Origin Private File System createWritable() throws NoModificationAllowedError under concurrent tab access and QuotaExceededError when limits are reached. Unhandled exceptions crash recording and playback.
antiPatterns: const writable = await handle.createWritable(); // without try/catch or fallback
OPFS_RESILIENT_STORAGE_FAILOVER.remediation: Wrap OPFS file operations with lock retry/backoff and fall back gracefully to MemoryStorageAdapter upon persistent lock contention or quota failure.

CROSS_SURFACE_PARAMETER_PARITY.summary: Studio API routes and UI controls must accept and forward all core pipeline parameters supported by the CLI.
CROSS_SURFACE_PARAMETER_PARITY.description: Dropping speed, verbalizeDiagrams, or custom voice parameters in parseNarrationRequest forces hardcoded defaults and denies users capabilities available via the CLI.
antiPatterns: return { id, markdown, voice, model, promptStyle, rewriteForNarration, visibility }; // speed dropped
if (!isVoice(raw.voice)) return null; // rejects valid custom voices
CROSS_SURFACE_PARAMETER_PARITY.remediation: Include speed, verbalizeDiagrams, and extensible voice support in NarrationRequest, and forward them from Studio routes to DocumentAudioPipeline.

DECLARATIVE_PROVIDER_REGISTRY.summary: Subsystems must dispatch model providers through a declarative registry rather than imperative hardcoded constructors.
DECLARATIVE_PROVIDER_REGISTRY.description: Directly instantiating new GeminiTTSProvider across CLI, TUI, sidecar, and Studio requires shotgun surgery to add alternative TTS or video providers.
DECLARATIVE_PROVIDER_REGISTRY.remediation: Provide a centralized ProviderRegistry / factory interface in src/tts/ and src/video/ that decouples provider instantiation from consuming callers.
